Eva: Trying to onboard a community model (hf://some-org/custom-chat) and the HF->Redwood conversion fails in the autoload step. stack: `TypeError: __init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'tokenizer_fast'`
Sanjay: ugh, that smells like a custom config class in config.json + auto_map mismatch. did the model ship with `trust_remote_code`-only code?
Eva: yep config.json has an `auto_map` entry pointing at `custom_chat.modeling:CustomChatForCausalLM` and the tokenizer is custom too. conversion script refused to import.
Kevin: reminder: Redwood conversion runs in a sandbox that disallows arbitrary remote code by default. `trust_remote_code=True` is needed for models that implement custom modeling/tokenizer classes. but that's a security callout.
Maria: Could you paste the top of config.json?
Eva: here's the snippet:
```json
"architectures": ["CustomChatForCausalLM"],
"auto_map": {
  "AutoModelForCausalLM": "custom_chat.modeling:CustomChatForCausalLM"
},
"model_type": "custom_chat"
```
Sanjay: OK. two issues we hit in the past: 1) HF's `auto_map` uses module import strings that sometimes require `:` vs `.` formatting depending on export—if our loader expects a different format import fails. 2) custom __init__ signatures may not accept the kwargs our conversion wrapper passes (e.g., we pass a `tokenizer` or `tokenizer_fast` kwarg).
Alex: quick repro on my laptop: calling `AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(path, trust_remote_code=True)` loads but then our conversion step that wraps the model into Redwood's runtime fails when trying to patch tokenizer special tokens.
Maria: Are there missing special tokens? I often see `special_tokens_map.json` or `added_tokens.json` shipped. If the tokenizer class is custom, `tokenizer.special_tokens_map` shape might differ.
Eva: The tokenizer is a custom tokenizer class that doesn't expose `bos_token`/`eos_token` attributes, only `start_token`/`end_token`. conversion expects standard names.
Sanjay: two pragmatic fixes: 1) set `trust_remote_code=True` during onboarding run so HF loads the custom classes; 2) add a small adapter that maps alias names (start_token->bos_token). e.g., after load: `if not hasattr(tok, 'bos_token') and hasattr(tok, 'start_token'): tok.bos_token = tok.start_token`
Kevin: also check `auto_map` format. HF supports mapping like `"AutoModelForCausalLM": "custom_chat.modeling.CustomChatForCausalLM"` vs with colon. try both.
Eva: tried both. With colon I get `ModuleNotFoundError` inside our isolated convert env; with dot variant `from_pretrained(..., trust_remote_code=True)` works locally but convert script still passes an unexpected kwarg to the class constructor.
Alex: can you paste the conversion error?
Eva: stack trace (trimmed):
```
TypeError: __init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'tokenizer_fast'
  File "/opt/convert/loader.py", line 142, in wrap_and_save
    model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(local_dir, trust_remote_code=True, **hf_kwargs)
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.10/site-packages/transformers/models/auto/auto_factory.py", line 765, in from_pretrained
    return cls._from_pretrained(...)
```
Maria: Looks like our wrapper is passing `tokenizer_fast` (a kwarg we added for internal tokenizers). Custom class __init__ doesn't accept it. We need a compatibility layer that filters unknown kwargs before instantiation.
Sanjay: Agreed. Patch idea: in conversion, detect if `auto_map` exists and if so, do a guarded import: `cls = _safe_import(path); sig = inspect.signature(cls.__init__); filtered = {k:v for k,v in hf_kwargs.items() if k in sig.parameters}` then call `cls.from_pretrained(..., **filtered)`
Kevin: That should work. Also document the security implications of enabling trust_remote_code in onboarding policy (explicit opt-in for model owners).
Eva: secondary problem: once I force-load with trust_remote_code and map kwargs, quantization run (8-bit) made outputs go weird on our chat eval. perplexity jump ~+18% and several hallucinations in knowledge benchmark.
Alex: was quant done with bitsandbytes + `load_in_8bit=True` or with GPTQ?
Eva: bitsandbytes 8-bit via `transformers` integration. baseline float32 -> q8: exact-match on our eval dropped from 74% -> 64% on Q/A set.
Sanjay: expected—custom operators sometimes aren't compatible with our per-token normalization. For custom models we need to re-run a small calibration eval before approving quant profile. Recommend trying 4-bit nf4 or GPTQ which sometimes preserves behavior better for custom heads.
Maria: also confirm tokenizer merges/byte-level differences after trust_remote_code load. If tokenizer changes byte-level encoding, that could explain quality regression post-quant. Compare tokenization of golden prompts: `tokenizer.encode(prompt, add_special_tokens=False)` between float and quant runs.
Kevin: note: we should capture the special_tokens_map.json and add explicit `pad_token`, `bos_token`, `eos_token` in conversion outputs so runtime doesn't infer them differently under quant.
Eva: action items for me: (1) update conversion wrapper to filter unknown kwargs for custom classes (Sanjay help), (2) add alias mapping for tokenizer special names, (3) add pre-quant calibration tests.
Sanjay: happy to own the wrapper patch. I'll make a draft PR with the `inspect.signature` filter and a small whitelist fallback.
Alex: I'll run a side-by-side: float32 vs q8 vs gptq on the eval suite and post metrics in #eng-ml-bench tomorrow.
Maria: I'm adding a small checklist to the onboarding docs: check `auto_map` format, require `special_tokens_map.json` or explicit token attrs, run small smoke eval before enabling quantization.
ml-ci-bot: CI queued: run model-convert-unit-tests (job 4821).
Eva: thanks all — will post new logs after the next CI run :rocket:
Kevin: :thumbsup:
